newsitem.title: UK: IEA SAYS FSU JUNE OIL SUPPLY FLAT AT 7.23 MLN BPD.
newsitem.headline: IEA SAYS FSU JUNE OIL SUPPLY FLAT AT 7.23 MLN BPD.

text.p: Oil supply in the Former Soviet Union (FSU) averaged 7.23 million barrels per day (bpd) in June, unchanged from May, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Friday.

Russian oil production rose 11,000 bpd to 6.12 million bpd in June from May's level and was remarkably steady during the second quarter, between 6.11 million bpd and 6.12 million bpd, the IEA said in its latest Monthly Oil Market Report.
Combined production of 3.82 million bpd from the top six Russian oil companies rose by 17,000 bpd in June.
The July output figure for Russia is estimated to to have fallen by 52,000 bpd to 6.07 million bpd.
Crude production in Kazakhstan in June averaged 489,000 bpd, a gain of 6,000 bpd from the downwardly revised may figure.
The Tengiz project produced 150,000 bpd, down 3,000 bpd on the previous month although production is still expected to rise to 187,000 bpd by the end of the year.
Azerbaijani crude production averaged 180,000 bpd in June of which 149,000 bpd was from offshore fields.
Exports from the Former Soviet Union countries rose to three million bpd in July a rise of 50,000 bpd from upwardly revised June levels.
Exports of oil products fell by 160,000 bpd in in July.

But seaborne crude oil exports, mostly from the Black Sea, rose by 250,000 bpd as favourable weather conditions and limited maintenance allowed increased amounts of Urals crude to meet demand created by the absence of Irai oil in the mediterranean market.

About 30,000 bpd of the seaborne crude exports was offset by lower Druzhba pipeline exports to Central and Eastern Europe where flodding reportedly led to precuationary reductions in refinery and pipeline operations.
Druzhba exports are now just 700,000 bpd or less than half of capacity following the reduction in June when the Leuna refinery in eastern Germany was taken out of service.
